topics.statement: Should homeschooling be seen as a valid and potentially superior alternative to formal schooling, or does keeping children out of school deprive them of important social experiences they cannot get at home?
topics.topic_label: Whether homeschooling is a good alternative to sending children to school
topics.position_a: Homeschooling is a valid and potentially superior alternative to formal schooling
topics.position_b: Keeping children out of school deprives them of important social experiences they cannot get at home

topics.statement: Should parents strictly limit their children's screen time, or does managing that balance teach kids self-regulation skills they will need as adults?
topics.topic_label: Whether parents should strictly limit how much screen time their children have
topics.position_a: Parents should strictly limit their children's screen time
topics.position_b: Managing screen time balance teaches children self-regulation skills they will need as adults

topics.statement: Should the government provide every adult citizen with a regular cash payment — no strings attached — to cover basic living costs, or is unconditional cash support an unaffordable and poorly targeted use of public money?
topics.topic_label: Whether every adult should get a regular no-strings cash payment
topics.position_a: The government should provide every adult citizen with a regular unconditional cash payment
topics.position_b: Unconditional cash payments to all citizens are unaffordable and poorly targeted

topics.statement: Should wealth taxes — annual charges on total assets like savings, property, and investments — be introduced as a way to reduce the gap between rich and poor, or are wealth taxes too difficult to enforce and too damaging to economic growth to be practical?
topics.topic_label: Whether annual taxes on total wealth would help reduce inequality
topics.position_a: Annual taxes on total assets should be introduced to reduce inequality
topics.position_b: Wealth taxes should not be introduced due to enforcement difficulties and economic harm

topics.statement: Should governments be required to publicly report each year on whether the gap between the richest and poorest in society is growing or shrinking, or is tracking inequality a distraction from simply improving conditions for those at the bottom?
topics.topic_label: Whether governments should publicly track the gap between rich and poor
topics.position_a: Governments should be required to report publicly each year on changes in inequality
topics.position_b: Tracking inequality diverts attention from directly improving conditions for the poorest

topics.statement: Should inheritance above a certain amount be heavily taxed to prevent wealth passing through generations, or does taxing inheritance punish families for saving and building something to pass on?
topics.topic_label: Whether large inheritances should be heavily taxed
topics.position_a: Inheritance above a certain amount should be heavily taxed
topics.position_b: Inheritance should not be heavily taxed regardless of the amount passed on

topics.statement: Should financial support for families — such as child benefit payments — be cut off after a certain number of children, or should support be available regardless of family size to protect children from poverty?
topics.topic_label: Whether child benefit payments should be capped by family size
topics.position_a: Financial support for families should be available regardless of the number of children
topics.position_b: Financial support for families should be cut off after a certain number of children

topics.statement: Should tipping be seen as a genuine act of gratitude that customers freely choose to give, or has it become an unfair way for businesses to pass their wage obligations onto customers?
topics.topic_label: Whether tipping is a free choice or an unfair burden on customers
topics.position_a: Tipping is a genuine act of gratitude that customers freely choose to give
topics.position_b: Tipping has become a way for businesses to pass wage obligations onto customers

topics.statement: Should wealthy individuals who donate large sums to charity be celebrated for their generosity, or does private philanthropy allow the rich to decide which social problems get solved in ways that should not be left to one person's preferences?
topics.topic_label: Whether billionaire charity giving does more good than harm
topics.position_a: Wealthy individuals who donate large sums to charity should be celebrated for their generosity
topics.position_b: Private philanthropy gives wealthy individuals undue control over which social problems are addressed

topics.statement: Should communities treat homelessness as a shared problem that everyone has some responsibility to address, or is a person's housing situation ultimately their own responsibility?
topics.topic_label: Whether homelessness is a shared problem or a personal one
topics.position_a: Homelessness is a shared problem that everyone has some responsibility to address
topics.position_b: A person's housing situation is ultimately their own responsibility

topics.statement: Should landlords be free to charge whatever rent the market will bear, or does owning multiple homes that others depend on come with a social responsibility to keep rents affordable?
topics.topic_label: Whether landlords should be free to charge whatever rent they like
topics.position_a: Landlords should be free to charge whatever rent the market will bear
topics.position_b: Landlords have a social responsibility to keep rents affordable

topics.statement: Should a person's financial struggles be treated as a private matter, or should communities create more openness around money so that people feel less shame in asking for help?
topics.topic_label: Whether people should talk more openly about money struggles
topics.position_a: Communities should foster more openness around money to reduce shame in seeking help
topics.position_b: A person's financial struggles should be treated as a private matter

topics.statement: Should newspapers and online news outlets be required by law to publish corrections in the same place and at the same size as the original story, or is it enough to leave correction policies up to each outlet to decide?
topics.topic_label: Whether news outlets must print corrections as prominently as the original story
topics.position_a: Newspapers and online outlets should be legally required to publish corrections in the same place and size as the original story
topics.position_b: Correction policies should be left to each outlet to decide without legal requirements

topics.statement: Should journalists be legally protected from being forced to reveal their sources in court, or should those protections be removed when national security is at stake?
topics.topic_label: Whether journalists can be forced to name their sources in court
topics.position_a: Journalists should be legally protected from being forced to reveal their sources in court
topics.position_b: Source protections should be removed when national security is at stake

topics.statement: Should whistleblowers who leak classified government information to journalists be protected by law if the information reveals wrongdoing, or should leaking classified material always be treated as a criminal act regardless of motive?
topics.topic_label: Whether leaking classified information to expose wrongdoing should be protected
topics.position_a: Whistleblowers who leak classified information revealing wrongdoing should be protected by law
topics.position_b: Leaking classified material should always be treated as a criminal act regardless of motive

topics.statement: Should people who are publicly criticised or "cancelled" online have any legal recourse against coordinated campaigns that damage their reputation, or is mass public criticism simply an unavoidable feature of free speech?
topics.topic_label: Whether people harmed by online pile-ons should have legal protection
topics.position_a: People harmed by coordinated online campaigns should have legal recourse against reputational damage
topics.position_b: Mass public criticism is a feature of free speech and should carry no legal liability

topics.statement: Should end-to-end encrypted messaging apps be required to give governments a way to access private messages in criminal investigations, or does building in that access fundamentally undermine everyone's privacy?
topics.topic_label: Whether governments should be able to access encrypted private messages
topics.position_a: Encrypted messaging apps should be required to provide governments access to private messages in criminal investigations
topics.position_b: Building government access into encrypted apps fundamentally undermines everyone's privacy

topics.statement: Should satirical content that mocks or impersonates real people be clearly labelled as fiction, or does requiring labels undermine the nature of satire and comedy?
topics.topic_label: Whether satirical content about real people must be labelled as fiction
topics.position_a: Satirical content mocking or impersonating real people should be clearly labelled as fiction
topics.position_b: Requiring labels on satirical content undermines the nature of satire and comedy

topics.statement: Should comedy and satire be allowed to target any group, religion, or community, or are some groups entitled to protection from mockery because of the harm that ridicule can cause?
topics.topic_label: Whether comedy and satire should be allowed to mock any group
topics.position_a: Comedy and satire should be allowed to target any group, religion, or community
topics.position_b: Some groups should be protected from mockery because of the harm ridicule can cause

topics.statement: Should anonymous accounts on social media be treated as equally valid voices in public debate, or does the ability to hide your identity make anonymous speech less trustworthy and less deserving of protection?
topics.topic_label: Whether anonymous social media accounts deserve the same voice as named ones
topics.position_a: Anonymous accounts should be treated as equally valid voices in public debate
topics.position_b: Anonymous speech is less trustworthy and less deserving of protection than identified speech

topics.statement: Should communities actively challenge and push back against hateful speech when they encounter it, or does engaging with hateful speech give it more attention and legitimacy than it deserves?
topics.topic_label: Whether communities should confront hateful speech or ignore it
topics.position_a: Communities should actively challenge and push back against hateful speech when they encounter it
topics.position_b: Engaging with hateful speech gives it more attention and legitimacy than it deserves

topics.statement: Should journalists be expected to remain strictly neutral and never publicly express personal opinions, or does pretending to have no point of view make reporting less honest rather than more honest?
topics.topic_label: Whether journalists should be allowed to share their personal opinions
topics.position_a: Journalists should remain strictly neutral and never publicly express personal opinions
topics.position_b: Journalists should be able to express personal views as concealing them makes reporting less honest
